ing: bone-in if possible, cut in large chunks
st: Put the beef, onion, bay leaves, garlic and [[1 tsp]] pepper in a large heavy pot.
Add about [[8 cups]] water so the meat is just covered. Do not salt yet.
Bring to a boil, skim off the foam, then cover and reduce to a low simmer.
Simmer 3 to 3.5 hours, topping up water as needed, until the meat falls apart.
Add [[2 tsp]] salt in the last 20 minutes.
Lift out the meat, discard the bones and bay leaves, and keep about [[1 cup]] of the broth.
Pound the meat in a bowl with a wooden mallet or masher, or shred with two forks, until stringy and fine.
Return the meat to the pot with the reserved broth and heat 10 minutes, stirring until the liquid is absorbed. Serve with pap or porridge.

ing: washed, stems trimmed; or collard greens
st: Wash the spinach well and chop it roughly.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Cook the onion and garlic 5 minutes until soft.
Add the tomatoes and cook 6 minutes until they break down into a sauce.
Add the spinach in handfuls with [[0.5 cup]] water, [[0.75 tsp]] salt and the pepper.
Cover and cook 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the greens are very tender.
Uncover and cook 3 minutes to reduce excess liquid. Serve with pap or meat.

ing: for frying, plus 1 tbsp for the dough
st: Mix [[3 cups]] flour, [[2.25 tsp]] yeast, [[0.25 cup]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Add [[1 cup]] warm water and [[1 tbsp]] oil and mix into a soft, sticky dough.
Knead 8 minutes on a floured counter until smooth and elastic.
Cover and let rise in a warm place for 1 hour until doubled.
Punch down and shape into 12 balls the size of golf balls.
Rest the balls on a floured tray, covered, for 15 minutes.
Heat [[4 cups]] oil to 340°F (170°C) in a deep pot.
Fry 4 balls at a time for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm, plain or split with jam or mince.

ing: grated; cantaloupe or honeydew stands in for wild lerotse melon
st: Whisk [[1 cup]] sorghum flour with [[1 cup]] cold water until smooth.
Bring [[2 cups]] water and a pinch of salt to a boil in a heavy pot.
Slowly whisk the sorghum paste into the boiling water.
Stir constantly, lowering the heat, for 5 minutes until it thickens.
Cover and cook on low for 20 minutes, stirring every 5 minutes, until the porridge is thick and soft.
Stir in [[2 cups]] grated melon and cook 5 more minutes.
Spoon into bowls, pour over [[1 cup]] warm milk and stir in [[2 tbsp]] sugar.

ing: whole, or use hominy or samp
st: Drain and rinse the soaked beans.
Put the beans and [[6 cups]] water in a large pot. Bring to a boil, boil hard for 10 minutes, then simmer.
Cook the beans for 45 minutes with the lid partly on.
Rinse [[1 cup]] sorghum and add it with [[2 cups]] more water. Simmer 45 minutes more, stirring now and then.
Meanwhile, cook the onion in [[2 tbsp]] oil for 6 minutes until golden.
Add the onion and [[1 cup]] corn to the pot.
Simmer 15 minutes until beans and grain are tender. Add water if it gets too dry.
Season with [[1.5 tsp]] salt and the pepper and serve hot.
Heat [[2 tbsp]] oil in a pot over medium heat.
Cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft, then add the garlic and chili for 1 minute.
Stir in [[1 tbsp]] curry powder and cook 1 minute.
Add the bell pepper and carrots and cook 5 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, [[1 tsp]] salt and [[1 tsp]] sugar and simmer 10 minutes until saucy.
Stir in the beans and simmer 10 minutes until thick.
Serve warm or cold with pap, bread or grilled meat.
